title: The Derivative as a Function
short: f′ gives the slope of f at every x.
trouble: Students sketch f′ to look like f, instead of tracking where f rises, falls and levels off.

blocks.html: Computing a derivative at a point one point at a time is slow. If we keep $x$ general instead of picking a number, the same limit produces a formula for the slope at every point. That formula is itself a function.

The derivative function is $$\role[slope at x]{rate}{f'(x)} = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\role[change in output]{output}{f(x + h) - f(x)}}{\role[change in input]{input}{h}}$$ for every $x$ where the limit exists. Its graph shows the slope of $f$: $f' > 0$ where $f$ rises, $f' < 0$ where $f$ falls, and $f' = 0$ where the tangent is flat.

blocks.name: derivgraph

opts.task: Move $x$ from left to right. The lower graph is drawn only where you have been: it records the slope of the upper graph.

blocks.cap: $f(x) = \frac{x^3}{3} - x$ on top, $f'(x) = x^2 - 1$ below. Turning points of $f$ line up with zeros of $f'$.

blocks.html: The slope of $f$ can be different at different points, so it depends on $x$: that is what makes it a function. The definition is the same limit as before, with $a$ replaced by a letter. Every formula you will learn in the next unit comes from evaluating this limit once, in general, so you never have to do it again for that kind of function.

blocks.title: A quadratic, in general
blocks.a: $f'(x) = 6x - 5$. For example, the slope at $x = 1$ is $1$ and at $x = 0$ it is $-5$.

blocks.title: A reciprocal, in general
blocks.a: $f'(x) = -\frac{1}{x^2}$, negative everywhere: $\frac{1}{x}$ falls on each side of 0.

items: Where $f$ climbs, $f'$ is above the axis; where $f$ falls, below.
At a peak or a valley of a smooth $f$, $f' = 0$.

blocks.html: Sketching $f'$ so that it looks like $f$: a peak in $f$ drawn as a peak in $f'$. A peak in $f$ is where the slope is 0, so $f'$ crosses the axis there. Check each turning point of $f$: it must line up with a zero of $f'$.
